title: Hyksos
capsule: The Hyksos (Egyptian hꜣw-ḫꜣswt, 'rulers of foreign lands') were a West Asian population—likely from the Levant—who settled in the Nile Delta during Egypt's Middle Kingdom and established the Fifteenth Dynasty at Avaris (modern Tell el-Dab'a) around 1650 BCE, controlling Lower Egypt and parts of the Delta during the Second Intermediate Period. They introduced the horse-drawn chariot, composite bow, and bronze weapons into Egypt, technologies that Egyptian rulers would later use to forge the New Kingdom empire. Ahmose I of Thebes besieged and captured Avaris around 1550 BCE, expelled the Hyksos, pursued them into Canaan, and thereby inaugurated the Eighteenth Dynasty and the New Kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Hyksos' core domain in the eastern Delta is archaeologically anchored at Tell el-Dab'a, but the full geographic extent of their political control into the Levant and upper Egypt is debated; the dataset's broad from/to spans reflect scholarly uncertainty about precise dates.
